content.text: {"persuasion":"PERSUADED","support_scope":"FULL","rationale":"The entry’s core identification—lamp oil as Spirit-produced, proven obedience rather than the Holy Spirit Himself—best explains the combined evidence. Ezekiel 36:27 distinguishes the indwelling Spirit as cause from walking in God’s statutes as result; Matthew 5:16 identifies visible light with good works; Proverbs 6:23 connects commandment, light, correction, and the way of life; and Matthew 25 presents oil as personally accumulated, exhaustible, nontransferable, and obtainable only before the decisive arrival. Those features fit a stored life of obedient response better than they fit the Spirit Himself. Exodus 25:6 and 27:20 also distinguish beaten lamp oil from compounded anointing oil, weakening the common transfer of Spirit symbolism from anointing passages. The modifiers in the entry are supported as a coherent symbolic synthesis: the oil is pressed or beaten, retained in vessels, and consumed to produce visible light. Although no single passage states the complete formulation verbatim, the specific Holy-Spirit counter-reading leaves more of the parable’s mechanics unexplained.","book_core_identification":"Lamp oil support_scope.description: Support for the exact glossary BOOK ENTRY only, never for the supporting chapter as a whole.

book_secondary_elaborations.description: Secondary assertions actually printed in the glossary BOOK ENTRY; exclude chapter-only claims.

unsupported_glossary_assertions.description: Material assertions actually printed in the BOOK ENTRY that the evidence does not support. Must be empty for FULL and nonempty for CORE_ONLY.

chapter_only_objections.description: Objections to applications or arguments found only in the supporting chapter. Preserved for later chapter review and excluded from the glossary scope ruling.
